questions.question: A particle starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration $4\,\text{m/s}^2$. Its speed after $5\,\text{s}$ is:
questions.explanation: Using $v=u+at$, with $u=0$, $a=4\,\text{m/s}^2$ and $t=5\,\text{s}$, we get $v=20\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.question: A projectile is thrown with speed $20\,\text{m/s}$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. Taking $g=10\,\text{m/s}^2$, its maximum height is:
A force of $10\,\text{N}$ acts on a body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$. The acceleration produced is:
questions.explanation: From Newton's second law, $F=ma$. Hence $a=F/m=10/2=5\,\text{m/s}^2$.

questions.question: A block of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is pulled horizontally by a force of $20\,\text{N}$ on a frictionless surface. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Since the surface is frictionless, net force is $20\,\text{N}$. Thus $a=F/m=20/5=4\,\text{m/s}^2$.

questions.question: A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving with speed $3\,\text{m/s}$. Its kinetic energy is:
A force of $10\,\text{N}$ acts on a body through a displacement of $5\,\text{m}$ in the direction of force. Work done is:
questions.explanation: $W=Fs\cos0^\circ=10\times5=50\,\text{J}$.

questions.question: A spring of force constant $100\,\text{N/m}$ is compressed by $0.2\,\text{m}$. The elastic potential energy stored is:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ moves in a circle of radius $1\,\text{m}$ with speed $4\,\text{m/s}$. The centripetal force is:
The escape velocity from the surface of Earth is approximately:
questions.explanation: The escape velocity from Earth is $v_e=\sqrt{2GM/R}$, approximately $11.2\,\text{km/s}$.

questions.question: Two masses $m$ and $m$ are separated by distance $r$. Their gravitational force is $F$. If the distance is doubled, the force becomes:
questions.explanation: Since $F\propto1/r^2$, doubling $r$ makes the force $F/4$.

questions.question: A simple pendulum has length $1\,\text{m}$. Taking $g=\pi^2\,\text{m/s}^2$, its time period is:
questions.explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}=2\pi\sqrt{1/\pi^2}=2\,\text{s}$.

questions.question: A wave has frequency $500\,\text{Hz}$ and wavelength $0.6\,\text{m}$. Its speed is:
questions.explanation: Wave speed is $v=f\lambda=500\times0.6=300\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.question: The electric field due to a point charge $q$ at distance $r$ is proportional to:
questions.explanation: From Coulomb's law, $E=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q}{r^2}$, so $E\propto1/r^2$.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance $5\,\mu\text{F}$ is connected to a $10\,\text{V}$ battery. The charge stored is:
questions.explanation: $Q=CV=5\,\mu\text{F}\times10\,\text{V}=50\,\mu\text{C}$.

questions.question: A $10\,\Omega$ resistor is connected across a $20\,\text{V}$ battery. The current through it is:
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law, $I=V/R=20/10=2\,\text{A}$.

questions.question: Two resistors $6\,\Omega$ and $3\,\Omega$ are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation: $\frac1R=\frac16+\frac13=\frac12$, hence $R=2\,\Omega$.

questions.question: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field. Its path is:
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity and acts as centripetal force, producing circular motion.

questions.question: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius $R$ carrying current $I$ and having $N$ turns is:
questions.explanation: For an $N$-turn circular coil, $B=\frac{\mu_0NI}{2R}$ at the centre.

questions.question: A coil has $100$ turns and area $0.01\,\text{m}^2$. It is placed in a magnetic field of $0.5\,\text{T}$. If the field changes uniformly to zero in $0.1\,\text{s}$, the average induced emf is:
questions.explanation: Average emf $=N\Delta\Phi/\Delta t=N A\Delta B/\Delta t=100(0.01)(0.5)/0.1=5\,\text{V}$.

questions.question: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential is increased when:
options: Frequency of incident light is increased
questions.explanation: $K_{\max}=h\nu-\phi=eV_s$. Therefore, increasing frequency increases the stopping potential.

questions.question: The number of moles present in $18\,\text{g}$ of water is:
questions.explanation: Molar mass of water is $18\,\text{g/mol}$. Thus moles $=18/18=1$.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element represents the number of:
questions.explanation: Atomic number $Z$ is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.question: Which orbital has the highest penetration among the following?
questions.explanation: For the same principal shell, penetration follows $s>p>d>f$. Hence $3s$ has greater penetration than $3p$ and $3d$.

questions.question: The most electronegative element is:
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale.

questions.question: Which molecule has a linear geometry?
questions.explanation: $CO_2$ has two electron domains around carbon and is linear with bond angle $180^\circ$.

questions.question: The bond order of $O_2$ according to molecular orbital theory is:
questions.explanation: The bond order of oxygen molecule is $2$, corresponding to a double bond.

questions.question: For an exothermic reaction, the value of $\Delta H$ is:
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat, so its enthalpy change is negative: $\Delta H<0$.

questions.question: If the equilibrium constant $K_c$ for a reaction is very large, the equilibrium mixture contains predominantly:
questions.explanation: A large $K_c$ indicates that products are strongly favoured at equilibrium.

questions.question: The pH of a neutral solution at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is:
questions.explanation: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, neutral water has $[H^+]=10^{-7}\,\text{M}$, so pH is $7$.

questions.question: The oxidation number of chromium in $K_2Cr_2O_7$ is:
The standard electrode potential of the standard hydrogen electrode is:
questions.explanation: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a standard reduction potential of exactly $0\,\text{V}$.

questions.question: During electrolysis, oxidation occurs at the:
questions.explanation: Oxidation always occurs at the anode, while reduction occurs at the cathode.

questions.question: For a first-order reaction, the unit of rate constant is:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, rate $=k[A]$, so the unit of $k$ is $\text{s}^{-1}$.

questions.question: The half-life of a first-order reaction is independent of:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, $t_{1/2}=\frac{0.693}{k}$, so it is independent of initial concentration.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ideal colligative property?
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure depends on the number of solute particles and is a colligative property.

questions.question: The oxidation state of oxygen in $H_2O_2$ is:
questions.explanation: In peroxides, oxygen has oxidation state $-1$.

questions.question: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.explanation: $Al_2O_3$ reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric.

questions.question: Which halogen is the strongest oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential among halogens and is therefore the strongest oxidising agent.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of $CH_3CH_2OH$ is:
questions.explanation: $CH_3CH_2OH$ contains two carbon atoms and an alcohol group, so its IUPAC name is ethanol.

questions.question: The major product of addition of $HBr$ to propene in the absence of peroxide is:
questions.explanation: In the absence of peroxide, HBr follows Markovnikov addition and gives 2-bromopropane as the major product.

questions.question: Which reagent is commonly used to oxidise a primary alcohol to an aldehyde under controlled conditions?
questions.explanation: PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) can oxidise a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without generally proceeding to the carboxylic acid.

questions.question: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes such as ethanal reduce Tollens' reagent and produce the characteristic silver mirror.

questions.question: The functional group present in carboxylic acids is:
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl functional group $-COOH$.

questions.question: The coordination number of the central metal ion in $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ is:
questions.explanation: Six $NH_3$ ligands are directly coordinated to cobalt, so the coordination number is $6$.

questions.question: Which ligand is a strong-field ligand?
questions.explanation: $CN^-$ is a strong-field ligand and produces large crystal-field splitting.

questions.question: If $z=1+i$, then $|z|$ is:
The coefficient of $x^2$ in $(1+x)^6$ is:
questions.explanation: The coefficient is ${}^{6}C_2=15$.

questions.question: If the roots of $x^2-8x+k=0$ are equal, then $k$ is:
questions.explanation: Equal roots require $b^2-4ac=0$. Thus $64-4k=0$, giving $k=16$.

questions.question: The sum of the first $20$ natural numbers is:
The determinant $\begin{vmatrix}3&2\\1&4\end{vmatrix}$ is:
If $\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|$, the angle between the two non-zero vectors is:
questions.explanation: Since $\vec a\cdot\vec b=|a||b|\cos\theta$, we have $\cos\theta=1$, giving $\theta=0^\circ$.

questions.question: The slope of the line joining $(2,3)$ and $(6,11)$ is:
The equation of the line passing through $(1,2)$ with slope $3$ is:
questions.explanation: Using point-slope form, $y-2=3(x-1)$, hence $y=3x-1$.

questions.question: The derivative of $\sin x$ is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x)=\cos x$.

questions.question: The maximum value of $4x-x^2$ for real $x$ is:
questions.explanation: $4x-x^2=4-(x-2)^2$. Therefore the maximum value is $4$.

questions.question: The value of $\int_0^\pi \sin x\,dx$ is:
questions.explanation: $\int_0^\pi\sin x\,dx=[-\cos x]_0^\pi=2$.

questions.question: The limit $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}$ is:
questions.explanation: The standard trigonometric limit is $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1$.

questions.question: The distance between $(0,0)$ and $(3,4)$ is:
The equation of the circle with centre $(0,0)$ and radius $5$ is:
questions.explanation: For centre $(0,0)$ and radius $r$, the equation is $x^2+y^2=r^2$. Hence $x^2+y^2=25$.

questions.question: The eccentricity of an ellipse is:
questions.explanation: For an ellipse, eccentricity satisfies $0\le e<1$. For a non-circular ellipse, $0<e<1$.

questions.question: If $\tan\theta=\sqrt3$ and $0<\theta<\pi/2$, then $\theta$ is:
questions.explanation: In the first quadrant, $\tan\theta=\sqrt3$ gives $\theta=\pi/3$.

questions.question: The principal value of $\sin^{-1}(1)$ is:
questions.explanation: The principal range of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$, hence $\sin^{-1}(1)=\pi/2$.

questions.question: The probability of getting a six when a fair die is thrown once is:
questions.explanation: There is one favourable outcome out of six equally likely outcomes, so probability is $1/6$.

questions.question: The mean of $2,4,6,8,10$ is:
The variance of a dataset in which every observation is equal to $5$ is:
questions.explanation: All observations are equal to their mean, so every deviation is zero. Hence variance is $0$.

questions.question: If $A$ is a $2\times2$ matrix and $|A|=3$, then $|2A|$ is:
questions.explanation: For a $2\times2$ matrix, $|kA|=k^2|A|$. Thus $|2A|=4(3)=12$.

questions.question: The general solution of $\frac{dy}{dx}=2x$ is:
questions.explanation: Integrating, $y=\int2x\,dx=x^2+C$.

questions.question: The area under $y=x^2$ from $x=0$ to $x=1$ is:
questions.explanation: $\int_0^1x^2dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\frac13$.

questions.question: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of $x^2-7x+10=0$, then $\alpha\beta$ is:
questions.explanation: For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, product of roots is $\alpha\beta=c/a$. Hence $\alpha\beta=10$.

questions.question: The number of ways of selecting $2$ objects from $7$ distinct objects is:
questions.explanation: The number of selections is ${}^{7}C_2=\frac{7\times6}{2}=21$.

questions.question: The value of $\log_{10}1000$ is:
If $f(x)=x^2+3x$, then $f'(1)$ is:
The value of $\int e^x\,dx$ is:
questions.explanation: Since the derivative of $e^x$ is itself, $\int e^x dx=e^x+C$.

questions.question: The value of $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}$ is:
questions.explanation: Using the standard limit, $\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}=\frac12$.

questions.question: If the vectors $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are parallel and non-zero, then their cross product is:
questions.explanation: $|\vec a\times\vec b|=|a||b|\sin\theta$. For parallel vectors, $\theta=0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, so the cross product is zero.
